title: Sizing Guide
subtitle: Learn about Elasticsearch cluster sizing concepts and Dell infrastructure options.

dataIngestion.title: Data Ingestion
dataIngestion.intro: Data ingestion volume is the primary driver for cluster sizing. The daily ingest rate determines storage needs across all tiers.
dataIngestion.bestCompression: DEFLATE codec, ~1.5x ratio. Best for warm/cold tiers with lower write throughput.
dataIngestion.defaultCompression: LZ4 codec, ~1.2x ratio. Good balance of speed and compression for hot tier.
dataIngestion.noCompression: No codec, 1:1 ratio. Maximum indexing speed, highest storage cost.
dataIngestion.overheadDesc: Elasticsearch adds ~10% overhead for indexing metadata, mappings, and doc values on top of raw data size.
dataIngestion.keyPointDesc: Start with an accurate daily ingest estimate. A 10% error compounds across tiers and replicas, potentially oversizing the cluster by 20-30%.

tierArchitecture.title: Tier Architecture
tierArchitecture.intro: Elasticsearch uses a tiered data architecture to balance performance and cost. Data moves through tiers as it ages via Index Lifecycle Management (ILM).

hot.name: Hot Tier
hot.desc: Active indexing and frequent queries. Uses fast SSD/NVMe storage with high memory-to-storage ratio (1:30).

warm.name: Warm Tier
warm.desc: Read-only data with occasional queries. Uses cheaper storage with lower memory ratio (1:160).

cold.name: Cold Tier
cold.desc: Rarely queried data kept for compliance. Minimal resources with memory ratio 1:500.

frozen.name: Frozen Tier
frozen.desc: Searchable snapshots on object storage (S3). Lowest cost with memory ratio 1:1600.

tierArchitecture.ilmDesc: ILM automates data movement between tiers based on age policies. Enable ILM to optimize costs by moving older data to cheaper storage tiers.
tierArchitecture.keyPointDesc: Not all tiers are required. Many deployments use only hot + warm. Add cold/frozen only if retention requirements exceed 90 days.

clusterSizing.title: Cluster Sizing
clusterSizing.intro: Cluster sizing determines the number and specifications of nodes needed to handle your workload.
clusterSizing.masterRole: Manages cluster state, index creation, shard allocation. Minimum 3 dedicated nodes.
clusterSizing.dataRole: Stores data and executes search/indexing operations. Sized per tier.
clusterSizing.ingestRole: Pre-processes documents before indexing. Needed for heavy pipeline usage.
clusterSizing.coordinatingRole: Routes requests, aggregates results. Needed for high search concurrency.
clusterSizing.jvmDesc: JVM heap is capped at 31 GB to use compressed ordinary object pointers (OOPs). Heap is set to 50% of available RAM, leaving the rest for OS file cache.
clusterSizing.keyPointDesc: The 31 GB JVM heap limit is a hard boundary. Exceeding it wastes ~32 GB of heap due to uncompressed pointers.

shardManagement.title: Shard Management
shardManagement.intro: Shards are the basic unit of data distribution in Elasticsearch. Proper shard sizing is critical for cluster stability and performance.
shardManagement.targetSize: Target shard size: 10-50 GB (50 GB recommended maximum).
shardManagement.maxPerHeap: Maximum 20 shards per GB of JVM heap memory.
shardManagement.replicaImpact: Each replica doubles the shard count. 1 primary + 1 replica = 2 total shards per index shard.
shardManagement.calculationDesc: The number of shards per index is calculated based on expected index size and the target shard size:
shardManagement.keyPointDesc: Too many small shards waste resources on overhead. Too few large shards limit parallelism and recovery speed. Aim for 20-50 GB per shard.

dellHardware.title: Dell Hardware
dellHardware.intro: ELK Sizer targets Dell PowerEdge servers with PowerStore FC SAN and PowerScale/ECS object storage.
dellHardware.computeDesc: Dell PowerEdge R-series rack servers provide the compute and memory for Elasticsearch nodes.
dellHardware.r660: 1U rack server, ideal for master/ingest/coordinating nodes with lower storage needs.
dellHardware.r760: 2U rack server, ideal for data nodes with higher storage and memory capacity.
dellHardware.mixed: Mixed configurations use R660 for infrastructure roles and R760 for data roles.
dellHardware.storageDesc: Storage is selected based on tier performance requirements.
dellHardware.powerstore: Fibre Channel SAN for hot/warm tiers requiring high IOPS and low latency.
dellHardware.powerscale: Scale-out NAS/S3 for frozen tier searchable snapshots.
dellHardware.ecs: Object storage for frozen tier with S3-compatible API.
dellHardware.keyPointDesc: Server model selection directly impacts rack space and power. R660 (1U) is 50% more rack-dense than R760 (2U) but has less expansion capacity.

sustainability.title: Sustainability & TCO
sustainability.intro: Sustainability metrics help estimate the environmental impact and total cost of ownership for your Elasticsearch deployment.
sustainability.pueDesc: PUE measures datacenter efficiency. A PUE of 1.5 means 50% additional power for cooling/infrastructure. Modern datacenters achieve 1.1-1.3.
sustainability.co2Desc: Annual CO2 is calculated from energy consumption and the regional carbon intensity factor (gCO2/kWh). Regions with more renewable energy have lower factors.
sustainability.tcoHardware: Hardware: Server, storage, and networking equipment costs (one-time, amortized over project years).
sustainability.tcoEnergy: Energy: Annual electricity cost based on total power draw, PUE, and regional electricity price.
sustainability.tcoLicensing: Licensing: Estimated Elastic license costs based on node count and tier.
sustainability.keyPointDesc: Energy costs often exceed hardware costs over a 5-year TCO. Optimizing tier usage and enabling ILM can reduce both cost and carbon footprint.
